title: Durable Claude launcher authority ports
description: Objective: make the landed @moe/runner Claude launcher composable with daemon-durable one-use grant consumption and launch registration without replacing its production runtime-pin, Job Object, lock, duplicate, and process-observation defaults. Deliverable: a narrow public launcher factory/port overlay that retains all production defaults except caller-supplied consumeGrant/registerLock authority ports, invokes those ports at the existing pre-open/post-start linearization points, and accepts only exact durable CAS/registration outcomes. Consumer: task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9. NOT in scope: daemon persistence, schema, claim/activation construction, HTTP ingress, provider policy, or changing the default launchClaude behavior. Current measured gap at HEAD 284d5dd: launchClaude accepts only an all-or-nothing ClaudeLauncherDependencies override; its defaults and constituent production ports are not public, while pre-consuming a grant causes GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED and leaving the pure default cannot durably close a crash between open and observation.
definitionOfDone: A public @moe/runner factory or overlay creates a Claude launcher that uses the shipped runtime pin, duplicate resolver, Windows Job boundary, OS lock, observation, clock and delay defaults while replacing only grant-consumption and launch-registration ports.

The injected grant port performs an exact one-use CAS at the existing pre-open grant phase; a committed UNUSED grant can advance once, replay/forgery/wrapper drift pins the exact delegated code and layer, and no physical open occurs on refusal or thrown/malformed fulfillment.

The injected registration port records the pending and observed process identities at the existing launcher phases; duplicate/restart delivery adopts or refuses from the durable registration before a second physical open.

All injected outcomes remain total under the landed descriptor/native-Promise containment and cleanup precedence; generated hostile cases assert positive cardinality, exact code/layer, open count, close/release order, and no secret echo.

@moe/runner root exports the factory/overlay and complete type closure; bare-root Node smoke uses real defaults with no deep import, focused runner typecheck/tests pass, and task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 is recorded as the production consumer.
taskRails: Preserve launchClaude default behavior for existing callers; do not export individual internal default ports or permit a caller to replace the Windows physical boundary piecemeal.
Use TDD; every refusal pins exact stable code and layer, and mutation drills prove the injected consume/register calls precede physical open/relaunch.
Use only public package roots across consumers; exact LF runtime bridges; target <=250 physical lines and split before 400.
No daemon/store code or test-owned authority in this runner task.

reopenReason: The overlay validates durable success arms only as standalone shapes, not as the exact success for the request issued. Production probes show an injected registration may return different lock/process identities and still decode OK, and an injected grant may return a different grantId/wrapper/version and still decode OK. At PREFLIGHT this can redirect the acquired OS lock before physical open. Add relational checks for both ports while preserving delegated refusal attribution, and pin well-formed-but-different hostile outcomes.

It runs twice: pending preflight, then real windows:pid:creationTime; persisting pending creates fake process authority and makes the real call conflict because priorRegistration is unchanged. Keep pure registerLock for validation/preflight and add a distinct injected commitProcessRegistration port invoked only after the started identity is proven. comments.author: architect-b1a46457
comments.content:
Planning decision on the two prior addenda, so neither reads as a silently narrowed DoD.

ADDENDUM 2 (comment-c1496f52, port shape) — ADOPTED IN FULL. The plan composes rather than replaces: pure `registerLaunchLock` runs FIRST at both existing phases and its outcome is returned verbatim unless REGISTERED; only then is the injected `commitProcessRegistration` called, with an explicit PREFLIGHT/STARTED phase. The launcher never decides what the daemon persists, so the daemon can reserve at PREFLIGHT and commit only the proven `windows:<pid>:<creationTime>` identity at STARTED — no fabricated process authority, and no pending row that would later refuse LAUNCH_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_REUSED as `priorRegistration`. `validateCommit` stays internal and pure; `consumeGrantDurably` is the distinct CAS. Both wrappers are synchronous. Both slots reuse the EXISTING PORT_KEYS entries — no new key, because `snapshotLauncherPorts` requires all ten and port-results.ts is already at exactly 250 lines.

One deviation from that addendum's suggested shape, measured rather than assumed: the overlay does NOT pre-run pure `consumeActivationGrant` before the CAS. `validateActivationCommit` provably does not intercept a replay — `initialGrantBinding` hardcodes state UNUSED / version 0 for the digest, so `deriveGrantId` reproduces the same grantId for a CONSUMED record and the replay reaches the grant phase. Pre-running the pure function there would answer replay from the PURE layer, leaving DoD 2's "pins the exact delegated code and layer" vacuous. Drill D1 in step 7 exists to prove that.

ADDENDUM 1 (comment-31ffc391, runtime-to-activation binding) — SPLIT OUT to task-de496f4785a242569aa4ffc3ef6f1d69, not dropped. The gap is real and I re-measured it: `grep -rn "runtimeObservationDigest" packages/runner/src/providers/` returns zero hits, `validateActivationCommit` never reads the field, and effect-activation.ts:215-217 already owns the authoritative PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_CHANGED mapping. It is excluded from THIS task because (a) task rail 1 forbids changing default launchClaude behaviour and a new ACTIVATION refusal does exactly that, (b) the written DoD never names it, (c) the description puts provider policy out of scope, and (d) its blast radius is separate fixture surgery — `COMMIT` is built at module scope from `makeActivationRequest()` whose runtimeObservationDigest is `DIGEST.runtime`, while `prepared` is built in `beforeAll` from a real temp executable, so the digests differ today and a naive guard reddens most of claude-launcher.test.ts. Daemon-facing note for whoever plans task-996e5318: a durable PREFLIGHT reservation must never be fed back into this launcher as `priorRegistration`. `registerLaunchLock` refuses on any non-null prior.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) ADD A NEW PORT KEY (e.g. `commitRegistration`) to PORT_KEYS — REJECTED. `snapshotLauncherPorts` requires every PORT_KEYS entry, so every existing caller and test that hands a full `deps` object (index-surface.test.ts:499, the fixture's `dependencies()`) would start returning null and the launcher would refuse. port-results.ts is also already at exactly 250 lines. The overlay merges into the EXISTING consumeGrant and registerLock slots instead — zero blast radius.

2) LET THE INJECTED PORT REPLACE `registerLaunchLock` OUTRIGHT — REJECTED, and this is the correction in comment-c1496f524e6241a1aaa327557f2c30d6. The daemon would have to reimplement claim binding, one-time-credential reuse and prior-conflict authority. The overlay COMPOSES instead: pure `registerLaunchLock` runs first at both phases, and only its REGISTERED outcome is handed to the injected port.

3) PRE-RUN pure `consumeActivationGrant` BEFORE the injected CAS — REJECTED. It would answer replay with GRANT_ALREADY_CONSUMED from the PURE layer, so the durable-replay test would be answered by an earlier guard and would stay green even if the injected CAS were deleted. DoD 2 requires the DELEGATED code and layer. `validateCommit` still runs upstream and is unaffected, and it provably does not intercept a replay (see codebaseInsights).

4) PERSIST THE PREFLIGHT `pending:` REGISTRATION AS PROCESS AUTHORITY — REJECTED (same audit comment). It fabricates a process identity and, once read back as `priorRegistration` on a restart, makes `registerLaunchLock` refuse LAUNCH_LOCK_CREDENTIAL_REUSED instead of adopting. The launcher therefore hands the port an explicit PREFLIGHT/STARTED phase and never decides what the daemon persists; the daemon may reserve at PREFLIGHT and commit only at STARTED. This is how DoD 3's 'records the pending and observed process identities at the existing launcher phases' is satisfied without inventing authority.

5) DISCRIMINATE THE TWO REGISTRATION PHASES BY INVOCATION ORDINAL — REJECTED. A counter silently mislabels if the launcher's call order ever changes. Classify on the process-identity prefix, with both call sites building the string from one shared constant so a format drift cannot pass.

6) THROW FROM `createClaudeLauncher` ON A MALFORMED AUTHORITY — REJECTED. Epic rail 4 wants a stable reason code. The factory returns a launcher that refuses CLAUDE_LAUNCH_AUTHORITY_UNUSABLE at LAUNCHER instead.

planningNotes.risks:
ORDERING / LAYER ATTRIBUTION
- The overlay wrappers run INSIDE existing containment: the preflight registerLock and the consumeGrant call sit inside `contained(...)` in claude-launcher.ts, and the post-start registerLock sits inside lifecycle's own try/catch. Do NOT add try/catch inside the overlay wrappers — you will swallow the throw and mislabel which layer answered. Keep both wrappers SYNCHRONOUS (audit comment: current store and launcher containment are synchronous).
- An authority port that returns a Promise must NOT be awaited. decodeGrant/decodeRegistration will see a non-record and yield MALFORMED, which is the correct fail-closed outcome (CLAUDE_LAUNCH_DEPENDENCY_THROWN/GRANT and CLAUDE_LAUNCH_LOCK_UNKNOWN/LAUNCH_LOCK). Assert it.
- Two layers can refuse registration (pure LAUNCH_LOCK, then the injected port). Epic rail 6: every refusal test must pin WHICH layer answered, not merely that it refused.

VACUOUS-TEST TRAPS specific to this task
- A replay test is vacuous if the overlay pre-runs the pure grant function. Drill D1 below exists for exactly this.
- 'Uses the shipped defaults' cannot be proven from an import list. Prove it by mutating a real primitive in its own file (drill D4).
- Type-only exports are invisible to index-surface.test.ts's Object.keys guard. Name every new type in the root `import type { ... } from "@moe/runner"` block and annotate a real value with it, or the type closure is unproven.
- A generated hostile matrix that produces zero cases passes. Pin a hand-written expected count.

- lifecycle.ts 249 / 250 and port-results.ts 250 / 250 have no headroom. The identity helpers go in claude-launcher-contract.ts (146) and REPLACE template literals in lifecycle.ts, so lifecycle should not grow. Measure with `grep -c '' <file>`; PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts.

rejectionHistory.reason: The overlay validates durable success arms only as standalone shapes, not as the exact success for the request issued. Production probes show an injected registration may return different lock/process identities and still decode OK, and an injected grant may return a different grantId/wrapper/version and still decode OK. At PREFLIGHT this can redirect the acquired OS lock before physical open. Add relational checks for both ports while preserving delegated refusal attribution, and pin well-formed-but-different hostile outcomes.
